title: GlobalFlows series book
note: Flexible catalog — hang series on layers; empty cell > fake number.

layers.label: Liquidity
layers.blurb: Fed plumbing, money markets, credit aggregates.

layers.label: Rates
layers.blurb: US curve, real yields, BEIs, MOVE, global 10ys.

layers.label: Risk
layers.blurb: Vol, credit spreads, financial conditions — fear and funding stress.

series.name: Fed assets
series.note: Fed's total balance-sheet assets. Rising = more liquidity into the system.

series.name: Bank reserves at Fed
series.note: Cash banks hold at the Fed. Falling reserves often mean tighter money-market conditions.

series.name: Overnight reverse repo
series.note: Overnight reverse repo — cash parked at the Fed. Drained to near zero since 2023, so the level no longer says much; the direction still does.

series.name: Treasury cash account
series.note: Treasury General Account — the government's Fed checking account. Rise pulls reserves out of banks.

series.name: Fed securities held
series.note: Securities the Fed holds outright (QE stock). Core of balance-sheet liquidity.

series.name: US money supply (M2)
series.note: Broad US money supply (cash, checking, savings). Slow growth can signal tight credit.

series.name: US bank loans & leases
series.note: Total bank loans & leases. Private credit still flowing to the real economy.

series.name: Credit impulse
series.note: Change in the YoY growth rate of bank loans (TOTLL). Rising = credit accelerating into the economy — the private-sector impulse, not just Fed plumbing.

series.name: Business bank loans
series.note: Bank lending to businesses. Soft = firms borrowing less or banks tightening.

series.name: US federal debt
series.note: Total US federal debt outstanding. Stock of government paper, not the monthly deficit.

series.name: China FX reserves
series.note: China's foreign-exchange reserves. Proxy for Asia USD liquidity and China capital flows.

series.name: ECB assets
series.note: European Central Bank balance sheet. Euro-area QE/QT pulse.

series.name: Bank of Japan assets
series.note: Bank of Japan assets. Japan still a huge global liquidity source.

series.name: SOFR overnight rate
series.note: Secured Overnight Financing Rate — US overnight secured funding cost. Higher = tighter cash.

series.name: Fed funds rate
series.note: Effective Federal Funds Rate — where overnight bank reserves actually trade vs the Fed target.

series.name: Net liquidity
series.note: Street shorthand: Fed assets − TGA − ON RRP. Rising = more cash in markets.

series.name: SOFR vs target top
series.note: Secured overnight funding minus the top of the fed funds target. Deeply negative means reserves are so ample that cash trades well inside the corridor; at or above zero means reserves are scarce — that is where repo broke in September 2019. A spread against policy cannot go stale as the balance sheet grows, so this is the most reliable read on plumbing.

series.name: Reserves ÷ GDP
series.sub: Bank reserves as share of GDP
series.note: Bank reserves measured against the size of the economy. The dollar figure always looks enormous, so the ratio is what tells you whether cash is genuinely ample: 6.9% when repo seized up in 2019, 16.6% at the QE peak.

series.name: Net liquidity ÷ GDP
series.sub: Net liquidity as share of GDP
series.note: Fed assets minus the Treasury account minus reverse repo, measured against nominal GDP. Same idea as reserves over GDP but counts the whole plumbing stack: 16.6% before the 2019 squeeze, 27.8% at the QE peak.

series.name: US 3-month yield
series.note: 3-month Treasury yield. Short-rate anchor near Fed policy.

series.name: US 2-year yield
series.note: 2-year Treasury yield. Highly sensitive to near-term Fed path.

series.name: US 5-year yield
series.note: 5-year Treasury yield. Mid-curve — mix of policy path and growth/inflation views.

series.name: US 10-year yield
series.note: 10-year Treasury yield. Benchmark long rate for mortgages, corporates, and risk assets.

series.name: US 30-year yield
series.note: 30-year Treasury yield. Ultra-long duration; sensitive to term premium and fiscal supply.

series.name: 2s10s curve
series.note: 10y minus 2y curve. Negative (inverted) often warns of slowdown; steepening can ease long-end conditions.

series.name: 3m10s curve
series.note: 10y minus 3m curve. Another recession-signal spread; deeper inversion = tighter credit impulse.

series.name: 5-year real yield
series.note: 5-year TIPS real yield. Cost of real (inflation-adjusted) money for the medium term.

series.name: 10-year real yield
series.note: 10-year TIPS real yield. Higher real yields = tighter financial conditions for risk assets.

series.name: 5-year inflation bet
series.note: 5-year breakeven inflation — market's expected average CPI over 5 years.

series.name: 10-year inflation bet
series.note: 10-year breakeven inflation — market's long-run inflation pricing.

series.name: 5y5y forward inflation
series.note: 5y5y forward inflation — inflation expected 5–10 years out. Fed's preferred long-run gauge.

series.name: Broad US dollar index
series.note: Fed broad dollar trade-weighted index. Stronger dollar = tighter USD liquidity abroad.

series.name: Real dollar index
series.note: BIS real effective USD — inflation-adjusted dollar strength vs trading partners.

series.name: German 10-year yield
series.note: German 10-year Bund yield. Euro risk-free long rate.

series.name: UK 10-year yield
series.note: UK 10-year Gilt yield. UK risk-free long rate.

series.name: Japan 10-year yield
series.note: Japan 10-year JGB yield. Global duration and BoJ policy pulse.

series.name: Bond volatility (MOVE)
series.note: ICE BofA MOVE — implied vol on Treasuries. Bond-market fear gauge (VIX for rates).

series.name: Dollar index (DXY)
series.note: ICE US Dollar Index vs majors (EUR, JPY, GBP, CAD, SEK, CHF). Classic DXY tape.

series.name: Euro vs dollar
series.note: Euros per dollar. Higher = stronger euro / weaker dollar.

series.name: Dollar vs yen
series.note: Yen per dollar. Higher = stronger dollar vs yen (often risk-off or rate-gap driven).

series.name: Dollar vs yuan
series.note: Offshore yuan per dollar. Higher = weaker CNH; China/EM stress tell.

series.name: Pound vs dollar
series.note: Pounds per dollar. Higher = stronger sterling.

series.name: Aussie vs dollar
series.note: Aussie dollar vs USD. Risk/commodity-linked FX.

series.name: Dollar vs peso
series.note: Pesos per dollar. Higher = weaker peso; EM stress proxy.

series.name: Sticky CPI
series.note: Atlanta Fed sticky CPI — prices that change rarely. Persistence of inflation.

series.name: Industrial production
series.note: US industrial production index. Factory and utility output pulse.

series.name: Nonfarm payrolls
series.note: Nonfarm payrolls — monthly jobs added. Headline labor-market print.

series.name: Unemployment rate
series.note: Unemployment rate. Rising = labor market cooling (soft for growth).

series.name: Initial jobless claims
series.note: Initial jobless claims — weekly new unemployment filings. Fast labor stress tell.

series.name: Continuing claims
series.note: Continuing claims — people still on unemployment. Stickier labor softening.

series.name: Job openings
series.note: JOLTS job openings. Labor demand; falling openings = cooling.

series.name: Quit rate
series.note: JOLTS quit rate. Workers' confidence quitting — high = tight labor market.

series.name: Average hourly earnings
series.note: Average hourly earnings. Wage pressure into inflation and margins.

series.name: Retail sales
series.note: Advance retail sales. Consumer spending pulse (nominal).

series.name: Durable goods orders
series.note: Durable goods orders. Capex and goods-demand lead.

series.name: Housing starts
series.note: Housing starts. New residential construction — rate-sensitive growth.

series.name: Building permits
series.note: Building permits. Forward look at housing starts.

series.name: Headline CPI
series.note: Headline CPI (all items). What households feel; noisy month to month.

series.name: Core CPI
series.note: Core CPI (ex food & energy). Fed's preferred CPI underlying read.

series.name: Headline PCE
series.note: Headline PCE price index — Fed's official inflation target basket.

series.name: Core PCE
series.note: Core PCE (ex food & energy). The Fed's main inflation target series.

series.name: Inflation expectations
series.note: UMich 1-year inflation expectations. Household inflation psychology.

series.name: Real GDP
series.note: Real GDP YoY. Volume of the whole economy — the real side of growth.

series.name: Nominal GDP
series.note: Nominal GDP YoY. Dollar spending in the economy — growth + prices. Split vs real GDP tells you how much of the heat is real vs inflation.

series.name: Nominal − real GDP
series.note: Nominal GDP YoY minus real GDP YoY. Wide = more of the expansion is prices; tight = more is real activity. Core for credit vs duration attribution.

series.name: Copper
series.note: Copper futures. "Dr. Copper" — industrial demand / global growth proxy.

series.name: Equity volatility (VIX)
series.note: Cboe VIX — 30-day implied vol on the S&P 500. Equity fear gauge.

series.name: High-yield spread
series.note: ICE BofA high-yield OAS. Extra yield junk bonds demand over Treasuries. Credit stress.

series.name: IG credit spread
series.note: ICE BofA investment-grade OAS. Extra yield on IG corporates — milder credit stress.

series.name: Financial conditions
series.note: Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index. Higher = tighter US financial conditions.

series.name: Adjusted financial cond.
series.note: Adjusted NFCI — strips out economic activity so it's more about pure financial stress.

series.name: S&P 500
series.note: S&P 500. Broad US large-cap equity risk appetite.

series.name: Nasdaq 100
series.note: Nasdaq-100. US mega-cap / growth equity tape.

series.name: Russell 2000
series.note: Russell 2000. US small-cap risk — more domestic and credit-sensitive.

series.name: Gold
series.note: Gold futures. Real-rate / dollar / fear hedge — treat as an output, not a cause.

series.name: Bitcoin
series.note: Bitcoin. Speculative liquidity-sensitive risk asset — output, not input.

series.name: WTI crude oil
series.note: West Texas Intermediate crude. US oil benchmark.

series.name: Brent crude oil
series.note: Brent crude. Global oil benchmark.

series.name: Stock–bond correlation
series.note: 60-day correlation of stocks vs bonds (sign-flipped). Rising together = less diversification.

series.name: Fed budget balance
series.note: Monthly federal budget balance. Deficit (−) means more Treasury issuance ahead.

series.name: Foreign Treasury holdings
series.note: Foreign holdings of US Treasuries. Soft = overseas buyers stepping back.

series.name: Fed Treasury holdings
series.note: Fed's SOMA Treasury holdings — the QE/QT Treasury piece of the balance sheet.

series.name: Debt held by public
series.note: Debt held by the public (ex Fed/gov accounts). The stock markets actually finance.

series.name: Fed funds target (top)
series.note: Top of the Fed's federal funds target range. Official policy rate ceiling.

series.name: Fed funds target (low)
series.note: Bottom of the Fed's federal funds target range. Official policy rate floor.

series.name: 30-year mortgage rate
series.note: Average 30-year fixed mortgage rate. Direct hit to housing and consumer duration.

series.name: 10y term premium
series.note: NY Fed ACM 10y forward term premium — extra yield for long-bond risk, beyond rate-path expectations.

series.name: 2y term premium
series.note: NY Fed ACM 2y forward term premium — near-term bond risk premium.

series.name: 10y vs fed funds
series.note: 10y yield minus fed funds. Positive steepness vs policy; compressed = tighter/longer-end caution.

series.name: Dollar vs franc
series.note: Swiss francs per dollar. Higher = stronger USD / weaker CHF safe-haven bid fading.

series.name: Dollar vs loonie
series.note: Canadian dollars per dollar. Oil- and NAFTA-sensitive cross.

series.name: Dollar vs real
series.note: Reais per dollar. Higher = weaker BRL; EM stress proxy.

series.name: Euro vs yen
series.note: Euro vs yen. Classic risk-on cross — rises when risk appetite improves.

series.name: Empire manufacturing
series.note: NY Fed Empire State manufacturing survey. Regional PMI-style activity.

series.name: Philly manufacturing
series.note: Philly Fed manufacturing survey. Another regional PMI-style read.

series.name: Chicago Fed activity
series.note: Chicago Fed National Activity Index. Broad monthly growth factor (0 ≈ trend).

series.name: Weekly economic index
series.note: NY Fed Weekly Economic Index. High-frequency real activity blend.

series.name: Case-Shiller home prices
series.note: Case-Shiller home price index. National house-price level.

series.name: Existing home sales
series.note: Existing home sales. Housing turnover — rates and affordability.

series.name: Consumer sentiment
series.note: University of Michigan consumer sentiment. Soft demand / mood gauge.

series.name: Commodity PPI
series.note: PPI all commodities. Upstream goods inflation.

series.name: Final-demand PPI
series.note: PPI final demand. Pipeline prices into consumer inflation.

series.name: Median CPI
series.note: Cleveland Fed median CPI. Robust underlying inflation (less noisy than mean).

series.name: Trimmed-mean CPI
series.note: Cleveland Fed trimmed-mean CPI. Another core-like inflation measure.

series.name: CPI shelter
series.note: CPI shelter. Housing rents/OER — big, sticky CPI weight.

series.name: Services CPI ex energy
series.note: CPI services ex energy. "Supercore" — services inflation the Fed watches.

series.name: Sticky core CPI
series.note: Atlanta Fed sticky core CPI. Core prices that are slow to change.

series.name: Baa spread over 10s
series.note: Moody's Baa corporate yield minus the 10-year Treasury - the extra yield demanded to lend to a middling company. Widening means doubt that borrowers pay. FRED computes this one rather than licensing it, so it carries 40 years of history and can be scored consistently across past cycles: 2.1 is the long-run median, 3.3 is where 2011 and 2016 topped out, and the 2008 peak was 6.07.

series.name: BBB credit spread
series.note: ICE BofA BBB option-adjusted spread. FRED's open download only carries three years of this one, so the risk light votes Moody's Baa over 10s instead, which reaches back to 1986.

series.name: CCC credit spread
series.note: CCC high-yield OAS. Distressed credit; blows out in risk-off.

series.name: Policy uncertainty
series.note: Economic Policy Uncertainty index. News-based US policy risk.

series.name: Sahm recession rule
series.note: Sahm rule trigger — unemployment jump vs recent low. Recession flag when ≥0.5.

series.name: High-yield bond ETF
series.note: iShares High Yield Corporate Bond ETF. Price tape for HY credit (up = easier).

series.name: IG bond ETF
series.note: iShares IG Corporate Bond ETF. Price tape for investment-grade credit.

series.name: Crash-insurance skew
series.note: Cboe SKEW — price of S&P crash insurance (tail risk). Higher = more fear of a crash.

series.name: Silver
series.note: Silver futures. Precious metal with industrial demand too.

series.name: Long Treasury ETF
series.note: iShares 20+ Year Treasury ETF. Long-bond price tape (up = yields down).

series.name: Brazil equity ETF
series.note: iShares MSCI Brazil ETF. EM equity risk proxy.

series.name: Developed ex-US equities
series.note: iShares MSCI EAFE. Developed equities outside the US.

series.name: Euro Stoxx 50 ETF
series.note: SPDR Euro Stoxx 50. Core European equity risk.

series.name: Japan equities
series.note: iShares MSCI Japan. Japanese equity risk appetite.

series.name: Emerging market equities
series.note: iShares MSCI Emerging Markets. Broad EM equity risk.

series.name: China large-cap equities
series.note: iShares China Large-Cap. China equity risk proxy.

series.name: High-yield bond ETF
series.note: SPDR Bloomberg High Yield Bond ETF. Credit risk as a traded price.

series.name: 7–10y Treasury ETF
series.note: iShares 7–10 Year Treasury. Intermediate duration prices.

series.name: 1–3y Treasury ETF
series.note: iShares 1–3 Year Treasury. Short duration / cash-like rates.

series.name: TIPS ETF
series.note: iShares TIPS Bond ETF. Real-rate / inflation-protected duration.

series.name: Platinum
series.note: Platinum futures. Industrial + precious metal.

series.name: Natural gas
series.note: Natural gas futures. Energy tape beyond oil.

series.name: Ethereum
series.note: Ethereum. Second crypto liquidity/risk proxy beside Bitcoin.

series.name: Dow Jones
series.note: Dow Jones Industrial Average. 30-name household US equity tape — narrower than the S&P 500.

series.name: Korea equities
series.note: iShares MSCI South Korea. Chip-cycle / export-growth equity tape.

series.name: India equities
series.note: iShares MSCI India. Large EM weight that was missing from the country set.

series.name: EM dollar bonds
series.note: iShares J.P. Morgan USD Emerging Markets Bond. EM credit as a traded price.

series.name: US aggregate bond ETF
series.note: iShares Core US Aggregate Bond. The whole investment-grade US bond market in one price.

series.name: Palladium
series.note: Palladium futures. Auto-catalyst metal — completes the precious/industrial set.

series.name: RBOB gasoline
series.note: RBOB gasoline futures. Downstream oil — the pump-price tape.

series.name: Heating oil
series.note: NYMEX heating oil / ULSD. Distillate — freight, heating, and the crack vs crude.

series.name: Dutch TTF gas
series.note: Dutch TTF natural gas. European gas benchmark — the non-US energy shock tape.

series.name: Corn
series.note: Corn futures. Global feed and ethanol grain.

series.name: Wheat
series.note: Chicago SRW wheat. Global food-grain tape.

series.name: Soybeans
series.note: Soybean futures. Protein / crush — China demand tell.

series.name: BNB
series.note: BNB. Exchange-chain crypto — liquidity-sensitive alt.

series.name: XRP
series.note: XRP. Cross-border payments crypto — beta to risk and regulation.

series.name: Solana
series.note: Solana. High-throughput smart-contract chain — crypto risk appetite.

series.name: TRON
series.note: TRON. High-volume settlement chain; often tracks crypto liquidity.

series.name: Hyperliquid
series.note: Hyperliquid. On-chain perp-DEX token — crypto trading-activity proxy.

series.name: Zcash
series.note: Zcash. Shielded privacy coin.

series.name: Dogecoin
series.note: Dogecoin. Meme-beta crypto — retail risk appetite.

series.name: Monero
series.note: Monero. Privacy coin.

series.name: UNUS SED LEO
series.note: Bitfinex LEO. Exchange-utility token in the large-cap set.

series.name: Chainlink
series.note: Chainlink. Oracle infrastructure — DeFi plumbing tape.

series.name: Cardano
series.note: Cardano. Large-cap proof-of-stake chain.

series.name: Stellar
series.note: Stellar. Payments-network crypto beside XRP.

series.name: Bitcoin Cash
series.note: Bitcoin Cash. Large-cap Bitcoin fork.

series.name: Litecoin
series.note: Litecoin. Classic large-cap crypto beside Bitcoin.

series.name: G4 central bank assets
series.sub: Fed + ECB + BoJ + PBoC, in dollars
series.note: The four balance sheets that actually set the price of global money, converted to dollars at market rates so they can be added up. The China leg is FX reserves rather than the PBoC balance sheet, which FRED does not carry — for global dollar liquidity that is arguably the more relevant number, since it is the part that recycles into world markets.

series.name: Global CB assets, 12m
series.sub: Are the big four adding or draining?
series.note: Year-over-year change in the G4 balance sheet in dollars. The level of a balance sheet grows forever and cannot carry a band; the rate of change is the thing that eases or tightens. Positive means the big four are net adding, negative means draining.

series.name: Dollar, 12m change
series.note: Most of the world borrows in dollars it does not print. A rising dollar tightens every one of those balance sheets at once, regardless of what the Fed is doing, which is why it belongs in the liquidity light and not just on the tape.

series.name: Global long rates (G3)
series.note: The average 10-year yield across Germany, the UK and Japan. Duration is priced globally: when Bunds and JGBs move, Treasuries follow, and a rates light built only from US yields mistakes a worldwide repricing for an American one.
